activity_context.topic_title: Representing 3x3 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+2y+8z=0 \\ 2x-5y+4z=3 \\ 5x-4y+7z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & a \\ 2 & b & 4 \\ 5 & c & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 8 \\ 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 8 \\ 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -4 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=8,\,b=-5,\,c=-4.$
